Flare start time: 2014-05-08T09:20Z.

## NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Space Weather Research Center ( SWRC )
## Message Type: Space Weather Notification - CMEs (STEREO A)
##
## Message Issue Date: 2014-05-08T03:18:36Z
## Message ID: 20140508-AL-001
##
## Disclaimer: NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center (http://swpc.noaa.gov) is the United States Government official source for space weather forecasts. This "Experimental Research Information" consists of preliminary NASA research products and should be interpreted and used accordingly.


## Summary:

Multiple CMEs have been detected as follows:
1: S-type CME detected by STEREO B / SOHO. 

Start time of the event: 2014-05-06T18:09Z.

Estimated speed: ~460 km/s.

Estimated opening half-angle: 47 deg.

Direction (lon./lat.): 108/5 in Heliocentric Earth Equatorial coordinates (see [1] in Notes).

Activity ID: 2014-05-06T18:09:00-CME-001

2: C-type CME detected by STEREO B / SOHO. 

Start time of the event: 2014-05-06T22:17Z.

Estimated speed: ~570 km/s.

Estimated opening half-angle: 32 deg.

Direction (lon./lat.): 103/-3 in Heliocentric Earth Equatorial coordinates.

Activity ID: 2014-05-06T22:17:00-CME-001

3: O-type CME detected by STEREO B. 

Start time of the event: 2014-05-07T16:39Z.

Estimated speed: ~1110 km/s.

Estimated opening half-angle: 41 deg.

Direction (lon./lat.): 122/-6 in Heliocentric Earth Equatorial coordinates.

Activity ID: 2014-05-07T16:39:00-CME-001

Based on preliminary heliospheric modeling carried out at NASA GSFC Space Weather Research Center, it is estimated that the CMEs may impact STEREO A.  The leading edge of the CMEs will reach STEREO A at 2014-05-09T17:33Z (plus minus 7 hours). 


Links to the movies of the modeled event (includes CME(s): 2014-05-06T18:09:00-CME-001, 2014-05-06T22:17:00-CME-001, 2014-05-07T16:39:00-CME-001):

http://iswa.gsfc.nasa.gov/downloads/20140507_015300_2.0_anim.tim-den.gif
http://iswa.gsfc.nasa.gov/downloads/20140507_015300_2.0_anim.tim-vel.gif
http://iswa.gsfc.nasa.gov/downloads/20140507_015300_2.0_anim.tim-den-Stereo_A.gif
http://iswa.gsfc.nasa.gov/downloads/20140507_015300_2.0_anim.tim-den-Stereo_B.gif
http://iswa.gsfc.nasa.gov/downloads/20140507_015300_2.0_anim.tim-vel-Stereo_A.gif
http://iswa.gsfc.nasa.gov/downloads/20140507_015300_2.0_anim.tim-vel-Stereo_B.gif


## Notes: 

This CME event (2014-05-06T22:17:00-CME-001) is associated with M1.0 flare with ID 2014-05-06T22:01:00-FLR-001 which peaked at 2014-05-06T22:09Z.

This CME event (2014-05-07T16:39:00-CME-001) is associated with M1.2 flare with ID 2014-05-07T16:07:00-FLR-001 which peaked at 2014-05-07T16:29Z.

[1] http://iswa.ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/wiki/index.php/Glossary/Heliospheric_Earth_Equatorial_coordinates

S-type: CMEs with speeds less than 500 km/s
C-type: Common 500-999 km/s
O-type: Occasional 1000-1999 km/s
R-type: Rare 2000-2999 km/s

## NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Space Weather Research Center ( SWRC )
## Message Type: Weekly Space Weather Summary Report for April 30, 2014 - May 06, 2014
##
## Message Issue Date: 2014-05-07T22:08:35Z
## Report Coverage Begin Date: 2014-04-30T00:00Z
## Report Coverage End Date: 2014-05-06T23:59Z
## Message ID: 20140507-7D-001
##
## Disclaimer: NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center (http://swpc.noaa.gov) is the United States Government official source for space weather forecasts. This "Experimental Research Information" consists of preliminary NASA research products and should be interpreted and used accordingly.


## Summary:

Solar activity was at low levels during this reporting period with two M-class flares (see list below).  There were five C-type CMEs (see details below).  The western flank of the CMEs starting at 2014-05-06T22:17Z and 2014-05-07T16:39Z are expected to arrive at STEREO A at around 2014-05-10T03:25Z (plus minus 7 hours).

Geomagnetic activity was at below minor levels with Kp index (a measure of geomagnetic activity, ranging 0-9) <=4 for the reporting period.   The Kp index reached 4 during the periods 2014-04-30T06:00Z-09:00Z and 12:00Z-15:00Z due to an extended period of southward interplanetary magnetic field possibly from a transient.  The Kp index reached 4 again during the period 2014-05-04T03:00-09:00Z due to the possible arrival of a CME starting at 2014-04-29T23:36Z, detected by ACE at L1 at 2014-05-03T16:48Z.  

The > 0.8 MeV energetic electron flux detected at GOES remained below the threshold level of 10^5 pfu for the entire reporting period, but was slightly elevated towards the beginning of the period.

The energetic proton flux of >10 MeV protons detected at GOES, and the 13-100 MeV protons at STEREO A and STEREO B were all at background levels for the entire reporting period. 

Space Weather Impact:
Space weather impacts on spacecraft are expected to have been low this week.
